Level 2 · Development Ages 8-10 Thinking workbook
JurassicEnglish.com · Thinking Expeditions
SAMPLE

EXPEDITION MAP Clue · Guess · Infer
Welcome to River Bend Camp!
River Bend Camp has tents, a muddy bank and a fossil table. Last night,
something tipped over a bucket. You ﬁnd out who on page 11.
I can …
I can tell what I see from what I guess.
I can use a clue to work something out. This is called inferring.
I can say what caused something.
I can write a claim and show the evidence.
Thinking words: seen guess clue infer cause effect claim
evidence because
Thinking Expeditions · Level 2 · Clue or Guess? 7
Hello, explorer! At River Bend Camp, strange things happen.
Today you are a clue hunter. You ﬁnd what you see. You ﬁnd
what is only a guess.

WATCH REX THINK Seen, inferred or guess: a worked example
Watch Rex think
Rex ﬁnds a footprint in the mud at the river bank. He says three things about it.
Rex's three sentences
The print has three toes.
The print is big, so a big animal probably made it.
The animal is very angry.
Seen Inferred Guess
My eyes tell me. A clue plus a careful idea. No clue.
The print has three
toes.
The print is big, so a big animal probably
made it.
The animal is very
angry.
Rex's questions: Can I see it? Then it is seen. Is there a clue and a careful idea
that the clue really helps? Then it is inferred. No clue? Then it is a guess.
Watch out: the word so can trick you. "The print is big, so the animal is angry"
is still a guess. A big print does not show anger.
Thinking Expeditions · Level 2 · Clue or Guess? 8
the footprint
 Rex's magnifying glass
First sentence: I can see three toes. That is seen. Second
sentence: the big print is a clue. I add a careful idea: a big
animal made it. That is inferred. Third sentence: I cannot see
any anger. I have no clue. That is a guess.

DIG Infer from evidence: seen, guess, inferred
Clue or guess?
1 A fact you can see is in the pictures. A guess is not. Write each number in
the right box.
1 The feather is blue. 2 Egg 1 is from a river animal.
3 Print 1 has ﬁve toes. 4 Print 1 is from last night.
5 Egg 1 has a crack. 6 The feather is from a dinosaur called Zip.
I can see it It is a guess
2 Three boxes now. Inferred = a clue you see + a careful idea (often so or
probably). Careful: so can trick you!
A The small animal is hungry.
B A small animal probably made print 2. C Egg 2 has a crack.
D Egg 2 is green, so it is from a long-neck dinosaur.
E Print 2 has three toes.
F Egg 2 has a crack, so the baby will probably come out soon.
Seen Inferred Guess
Thinking Expeditions · Level 2 · Clue or Guess? 9
feather
 egg 1
 print 1
 print 2
 egg 2

DIG Cause and effect: what happened, and why?
Cause and effect
Cause (why) Effect (what
happened) Rex's sentence
Bao dropped his brush in
the river.
The brush ﬂoated
away.
The brush ﬂoated away because Bao
dropped it.
Omar rang the camp bell. Everybody came to the
tent.
Everybody came because Omar rang
the bell.
Effects
A The egg has a crack.
B Rex's hat ﬂew away.
C The bucket is full of water.
D The mud is dry.
3 Match each cause to its effect. Write the letter A, B, C or D.
Cause Effect letter
1 Nia left the bucket in the rain.
2 Bao dropped a fossil egg on a rock.
3 The sun was hot all day.
4 The wind blew very hard.
4 Rain fell all night, so the path was muddy. Which part is the effect?
Rain fell all night. The path was muddy.
5 Your turn! Write what happened and why.
because .
Thinking Expeditions · Level 2 · Clue or Guess? 10
A cause tells why. An effect tells what happened.

WEIGH Cite evidence: rule in, rule out
The tipped bucket
Case: Who tipped the bucket?
1 The bucket is on its side by the fossil table.
2 Wet prints go from the river to the table.
3 The prints are small. Each print has three toes.
4 The air is still today. Not one tent ﬂap moves.
5 Bumbo is big. His feet have ﬁve toes.
6 Pip is small. His feet have three toes.
6 Who most likely tipped the bucket?
Pip Bumbo the wind
7 Write in or out. Then write the sentence numbers that tell you.
Suspect In or out? Sentences
Pip
Bumbo
The wind
8 Does sentence 2 tell you who tipped the bucket?
Yes, the prints show who it was.
No, it only says where the prints go.
Thinking Expeditions · Level 2 · Clue or Guess? 11
Pip
 Bumbo
 print at the table

BECAUSE Claim + evidence; more than one good answer
Claim and evidence
Claim (what I think) Evidence (the clue)
The egg will hatch soon. I can see a crack in the egg.
9 Look back at the case on page 11. Write your claim and your evidence.
My claim: tipped the bucket.
Evidence 1: Sentence says .
Evidence 2: Sentence says .
10 Bao ﬁnds a blue feather by the river. Where did it come from? Give one
good idea.
I think because .
Thinking Expeditions · Level 2 · Clue or Guess? 12
A claim is what I think. Evidence is the clue that shows it. A good
thinker gives both.
Sometimes more than one explanation is good. Then your clue
matters most.
the blue feather

CHALLENGE FOSSIL Evidence beats a guess
The missing egg
 Challenge fossil
Case: Who took the egg? Read the clue cards.
Clue card What it says
Nest Last night the nest on the rock had three eggs. Now it has two.
Feather There is a blue feather in the nest.
Omar Omar says, "I guess Rolo took it."
Rolo Rolo is a big long-neck. He has no feathers.
Zip Zip is a small ﬂyer. Zip has blue feathers.
Prints There are no big prints near the rock.
11 Who most likely took the egg?
Zip Rolo nobody
12 Which clue card is only a guess?
Nest Omar Prints
13 Which two clue cards are the best evidence for Zip?
Feather and Zip Nest and Omar Rolo and Prints
14 Write your claim with two pieces of evidence.
Claim: took the egg.
Evidence 1: The card says .
Evidence 2: The card says .

egg
 egg
feather from
the nest
 Zip

STORY LINK Use the thinking on a short story
Nia's wet boots
Morning at River Bend
Nia wakes up at River Bend Camp. Her boots are by the tent door. The
boots are full of mud.
Nia thinks, "The river came up in the night."
Bao says, "A river monster took my hat!"
Nia looks at the bank. The mud is high and wet. The water is near the tents.
15 Which part is only a guess?
The boots are full of mud. A river monster took my hat!
The mud is high and wet.
16 Nia thinks the river came up. Which words are the best evidence?
Nia wakes up at River Bend Camp. A river monster took my hat!
The mud is high and wet. The water is near the tents.
Storybook hunt: open any Level 2 Jurassic English storybook. Find one clue in
a picture or in the words. Find one guess a character makes.
17 Write what you found.
A clue I found:
A guess a character makes:
The book is called:
Thinking Expeditions · Level 2 · Clue or Guess? 14
Your turn! A good author hides clues in a story. Be a clue hunter
in a storybook.

SHOW WHAT I KNOW Unit check: do it alone
Show what I know
18 Look at the tooth. Which one is a guess?
The tooth is sharp. There is one tooth in the picture.
The animal with this tooth was happy.
19 Which sentence is inferred (a clue plus a careful idea)?
The tooth is sharp.
The tooth is sharp, so the animal is a happy dinosaur.
The tooth is sharp, so the animal probably ate meat.
20 The rug is wet because ___. Which is the cause?
Nia spilled her water. The rug is long. Omar is tall.
An apple was on the fossil table. Now it is gone.
Big prints with ﬁve toes are by the table.
Tank is big. His feet have ﬁve toes.
Pip is small. His feet have three toes.
21 Read the case. Who most likely took the apple?
Tank Pip We cannot tell
22 Write your claim and your evidence.
I think took the apple.
Evidence (copy the exact words): " "
Thinking Expeditions · Level 2 · Clue or Guess? 15
the tooth

THINKING MIRROR How did my brain do?
Thinking mirror
Colour 1, 2 or 3. 1 = not yet, 2 = getting there, 3 = I can do it.
I can … How sure am I?
I can tell what I see from what I guess. 1 2 3
I can use a clue to work something out (infer). 1 2 3
I can say the cause and the effect. 1 2 3
I can show my evidence with a clue, a card or exact words. 1 2 3
I can write a claim and its evidence. 1 2 3
The best clue I found today (draw it and say why it is a clue):
Finish the sentence.
Next time I will check before I say an answer.
Grown-up's note: ask, 'What is your clue?' Listen for because and the exact
words from the page. Praise the clue, not just the answer.
Thinking Expeditions · Level 2 · Clue or Guess? 16
Great digging, clue hunter! Now look at your own thinking.
